sources_read: .qc-cache/coldwater-strict-2026-10-08-v16-quick4/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx (Quality Checks sheet row 5 and the matching sheet4 row; no internal annotation on this row)
evidence: Ran the skill's grep (judge|rubric|grader|grading|score|scoring|weight|dimension|/tests|test.sh|verifier|reward|sentinel|harbor|oracle|playwright|criteri|checker|evaluat|cw_|mcp|test) case-insensitively over instruction.md, all six notes and seed_data.json: zero hits. None of the 55 criterion ids from tests/*/*/judge.toml appears in any public file (grep -F -f ids: exit 1). The only uppercase tokens shared with tests/ are DB_PATH and NODE_PATH, which are runtime-contract facts (integration.md). No probe literal, dimension name (render/constraints/functional/polish/visual as grading axes), weight, restart_app tool, Playwright or app_context.md path appears. Shingle comparison of the public text against every tests/*.md and *.toml: no shared 10-word run; at 7 words only two incidental fragments ('selection ends at the very start of the' in functional judge.toml, 'the preview the console and the library' in polish judge.toml), which are criteria quoting the request rather than the brief exposing criteria. The frozen task tree is byte-identical to the working-tree project at HEAD 5e036ba0 (diff -rq empty). 'Please check it yourself the way I'll use it' in instruction.md is ordinary requester advice and names no grader mechanics. Commit 5e036ba0's rewritten overview/policy/security/integration notes add no grader vocabulary. Cross-check of the four portal patterns: (1) all six notes are first-person requester prose with no numbered acceptance list or shall/must table; (25) no prompt or criterion sends the judge to a public address; app_context.md:27 says no criterion needs an address outside this machine, and every external reference is an 'external CDN requests are allowed' allowance; (32) all four Stop/supersede timing criteria (cw_output_before_failure_kept, cw_last_good_recovery, cw_stop_cancels_pending_work, cw_newer_run_supersedes) share the same rule: a void attempt, up to two more, and fail only if every attempt is void; (35) cw_save_reload_restart now requires two saves, an in-app restore creating revision three, a real restart_app restart, a re-read of all revisions, and a replayed restore that must add no revision. Nothing got looser for the model on this row. The void rules apply only to judge-side timing (the old marker appearing before the newer Run, or the start line not appearing within about 2s), and an app that fires timers early still ends in a fail. A weak app cannot gain anything here because the row concerns the brief only. A conforming app cannot be hurt by this row. Observation for other rows, not a row-5 defect: the post-restart replay expects restore idempotency to survive a process restart. behaviour.md supports this ('arrives again after it already went through', plus history surviving restart), but an app with an in-memory idempotency cache would fail it, so whoever owns rows 6 and 35 should confirm that reading.
